findings.claim: Wave decision W2-005 says 'a GET with Upgrade: websocket resolves only against WebSocket routes and a plain request only against HTTP routes'. Read literally, an Upgrade: websocket GET to a path that has only a GET route finds no WebSocket route and returns no-match, which contradicts frozen D-441 (the loop-D carried fix): such a request is resolved as an ordinary GET and reaches the path's GET registration, else method-mismatch or no-match. The section claims to 'contradict no frozen item'.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword W2-005: an Upgrade: websocket GET resolves against WebSocket routes first; if no WebSocket pattern matches the path it falls back to HTTP routes as an ordinary GET (D-441). A plain request resolves only against HTTP routes, apart from the WebSocket-only check of D-069.

findings.claim: Wave decision W2-004 lists 'automatic HEAD method value' among the docs/api/routing.md markers that wave 2 removes under D-070. Frozen D-398 gives wave 3 the decision on the value of req.method() during automatic HEAD and the removal of that marker (routing.md:119). D-070 does not list it. So W2-004 moves a wave-3 decision into wave 2. Also, the //, trailing-slash, case and TRACE/CONNECT markers in routing.md are the only ones W2-004 names, and they are config-API name markers (routing.md:71,91) that it already leaves for D-398. Wave 2 then has no marker it can rightly remove, so 'removes only ... markers' is misleading.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop 'automatic HEAD method value' from W2-004. State that wave 2 writes the decided //, trailing-slash, case and TRACE/CONNECT semantics into routing.md and leaves the 설정 API (미확정) markers and the req.method() marker for wave 3 (D-398).

findings.claim: W2-001 limits WebSocket-only (426) to a GET without Upgrade. Every other method on a WebSocket-only path then gets automatic OPTIONS or 405. This resolves the r1 overlap, but it narrows D-069 ('a request without Upgrade', any method), and the section's 'contradict no frozen item' claim does not acknowledge that. Also left open: whether a WebSocket route adds GET, automatic HEAD or OPTIONS to the Allow union of W2-002, and so what Allow a POST or OPTIONS to a WebSocket-only path returns.
findings.suggested_fix: State explicitly that D-069 applies to GET (the method a handshake uses) and that other methods fall under D-061/D-064. Say whether WebSocket routes count toward the Allow set (e.g. Allow: GET, OPTIONS for a WebSocket-only path), and cover it in a router test.
